candidate.blueprint_locator: Physiological Integrity — Reduction of Risk Potential: obtain diagnostic specimens correctly, monitor for infection-related complications, and use laboratory results to reduce risk.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — wound culture specimen quality
candidate.educational_objective: When a wound swab culture is indicated, obtain the specimen from cleansed viable wound-bed tissue using pressure to express tissue fluid and avoid superficial exudate or necrotic material so the result better represents clinically relevant organisms.

options.A: Cleanse the wound, select viable wound-bed tissue, and rotate the swab over about 1 cm² with enough pressure to express wound fluid while avoiding pus, slough, eschar, necrotic material, and surface exudate.
options.B: Collect drainage from the surrounding skin before cleansing because surface exudate best represents organisms in viable wound tissue.
options.C: Swab necrotic tissue preferentially because devitalized material provides the most accurate sample of the organisms driving invasive infection.
options.D: Skip wound-bed assessment and culture every chronic wound routinely because bacterial growth on a swab confirms that the wound is infected.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. Current NCBI nursing guidance for wound-culture collection directs the nurse to irrigate and cleanse the wound to remove surface debris, identify approximately 1 cm² of viable tissue, and rotate the swab over that area with sufficient pressure to express wound fluid. The specimen should not be taken from pus, slough, eschar, necrotic tissue, or skin exudate. B and C increase the chance of sampling surface colonizers or nonviable material rather than the clinically relevant wound bed. D is incorrect because wound cultures are obtained when infection is suspected and bacterial presence on a chronic wound does not by itself establish clinical infection. Tissue sampling may be preferred when deeper or more definitive microbiologic assessment is needed.
candidate.source_claim_supported: For an indicated wound swab culture, cleansing followed by pressure swabbing of viable wound-bed tissue yields a more clinically appropriate specimen than superficial exudate or necrotic material; the culture result must still be interpreted in clinical context.
candidate.source_document_title: Nursing Skills — Chapter 20 Wound Care, 20.9 Checklist for Wound Culture
candidate.source_locator: Section 20.9 Checklist for Wound Culture, steps 9–20: irrigate with sterile normal saline to remove surface debris/exudate; wipe surface contaminants; identify a 1-cm² area of viable wound tissue; do not sample pus, slough, eschar, or necrotic tissue; rotate swab over the selected area for 5 seconds with sufficient pressure to express wound fluid; never collect exudate from the skin.
